problem: Residents in small neighborhoods want to exchange books locally but lack a simple way to list, request, and schedule pickups, leading to missed sharing opportunities and cluttered group chats.
solution: A lightweight static web app where users can post books they offer, browse nearby offers, send pickup requests, and track pending exchanges, all stored in the browser with optional export/import for persistence.

competitors.name: BookCrossing
competitors.difference: Focuses on global tracking; no neighborhood‑only UI or simple static hosting.

competitors.name: Nextdoor
competitors.difference: General social platform; no dedicated book‑swap workflow or offline‑first design.

features: Add a book listing with title, author, condition, and optional photo
Search and filter listings by title or genre
Request a pickup; the owner can accept or decline
Local storage of all data; export/import JSON for backup or sharing
Responsive design for mobile and desktop

monetization.pricing_hypothesis: Offer premium features like QR code labels and custom themes for $2/month after 500 active users.
monetization.free_tier: All core listing, search, and request features remain free.

operating_costs: Current prototype: ₹0 within published free-tier limits
launch_strategy: Create a simple landing page and share in local community newsletters and Nextdoor groups.
Collect feedback via a short survey linked from the site.
Iterate based on user input before adding premium options.

marketing_content.tagline: Turn your shelves into community shelves.
marketing_content.social_post: 📚 Introducing Neighborhood BookSwap – a free, offline‑first way to list, request, and exchange books right in your block. No login, no ads, just reading. Try it now at https://yourusername.github.io/neighborhood-bookswap

tests: Add a new book, refresh page, verify it persists via localStorage.
Search for a title that exists, ensure results show the correct card.
Send a pickup request, accept it, and confirm status changes to 'Accepted'.
next_improvements: Add QR code generation for each listing to simplify in‑person handovers.
Implement a lightweight serverless function for optional cloud backup.
Introduce user‑generated tags for better categorization.
